arguments.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a dated tarball and copies it to the destination.
set -eu

# Set BACKUP_DEST to either a mounted/local destination or an scp destination
# (for example, /mnt/backups or backup.example:/srv/backups).  A destination is
# deliberately required: silently falling back to a local directory can leave
# a nightly backup on the job host rather than at the backup site.
DEST=${BACKUP_DEST:-${1:-}}
if [ -z "$DEST" ]; then
    echo "backup.sh: set BACKUP_DEST (or pass the backup destination as the first argument)" >&2
    exit 2
fi

SCRIPT_DIR=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)
STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="$SCRIPT_DIR/logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

tar -C "$SCRIPT_DIR" -czf "$BUNDLE" logs/

# A colon denotes the host:path syntax accepted by scp; otherwise the
# destination is assumed to be a mounted or local filesystem path.
case "$DEST" in
    *:*) scp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST" ;;
    *)   cp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST" ;;
esac

echo "wrote $BUNDLE and copied it to $DEST"

# A colon denotes the host:path syntax accepted by scp; otherwise the

arguments.command:
set -eu
rm -f logs-*.tar.gz
out=$(mktemp -d)
BACKUP_DEST="$out" ./backup.sh
test -f "$out/logs-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz"
tar -tzf "$out/logs-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz" | grep -Fx 'logs/app.log'
tar -tzf "$out/logs-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz" | grep -Fx 'logs/error.log'
set +e
./backup.sh >/tmp/backup.out 2>/tmp/backup.err
status=$?
set -e
test "$status" -eq 2
grep -F 'set BACKUP_DEST' /tmp/backup.err
rm -f logs-*.tar.gz
rm -rf "$out"
printf 'backup tests passed\n'
sh -n backup.sh
